newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Land fund could pressure HK dollar peg - sources.
newsitem.headline: Land fund could pressure HK dollar peg - sources.

text.p: A decision on how Hong Kong will manage the vast Special Administrative Region (SAR) land fund, which holds about HK$150 billion in land revenues, could be influenced by its effect upon the Hong Kong dollar, government sources said on Wednesday.
"They are so huge ... they could affect the exchange rate," the source said.
The SAR land fund will be folded into government revenues after the handover at midnight on June 30, when British rule ends and Hong Kong becomes an SAR of China.

How the money will be managed is still up in the air. Hong Kong officials, including Financial Secretary Donald Tsang and Hong Kong Monetary Authority chief Joseph Yam, argue the funds should be with the Hong Kong Exchange Fund, the reserves used to back the Hong Kong dollar.
Hong Kong has pegged its currency at HK$7.80 to the U.S. dollar.
If Hong Kong places the entire land fund in with the Exchange Fund, the Hong Kong dollar could strengthen and pressure the peg, the sources said.
The government of the Hong Kong SAR will be required to make a decision on the fate of the land fund, which was created in 1983 to hold revenues from land sales before China took back Hong Kong.
Half of all revenues went directly to the Hong Kong government. The other half was held in trust and will be handed to the Hong Kong SAR when it comes into being.
